tool.name: bfs_crawl
tool.description:
Breadth-first crawl of a web target with JS-bundle endpoint extraction and OpenAPI consumption.
The agent's natural depth-first improvisation through a SPA misses most of the attack surface — it lives bundled inside JS files the agent never reaches. This tool runs a deterministic breadth-first crawl, mines JS bundles for path-shaped string literals (LinkFinder-style), parses any supplied OpenAPI spec, and produces a flat endpoint inventory for the rest of the web-app team to pivot off.
Composes with the cluster-A safety middleware: every fetch goes through the same path that honors `--auth-cookie` / `--auth-bearer` / `--auth-basic` / `--header` (auto-inject) + `--exclude-path` (hard skip BEFORE dispatch) + `--rate-limit` (throttle). The agent does not need to thread credentials through manually.
Use this near the start of any web_application target: 1. (External step) `fingerprint_tech_stack(target)` first — auto-loads framework skills. 2. **This tool** — produces the endpoint inventory. 3. The agent enters exploit phase, picking endpoints to attack from the inventory.
Typical use after a domain-target handoff: `spawn_webapp_subteam` (#34) gives each sub-agent a single in-scope subdomain; the sub-agent's first move is `bfs_crawl` on that host.
Output is deterministic — same input + same target state = same endpoint list.

parameter.name: target
parameter.description: The in-scope target URL. Plain hostnames get https:// prefixed automatically.

parameter.name: max_pages
parameter.description: Cap on pages visited. Default 200, hard-capped at 2000. Each page costs 1 request (subject to rate-limit).

parameter.name: max_depth
parameter.description: BFS depth cap. Default 3, hard-capped at 8. Most app surface lives at depth ≤ 3 from the homepage.

parameter.name: seed_urls
parameter.description: Comma-separated extra start URLs in addition to the target. CLI: `--seed-url` (repeatable) sets `STRIX_SEED_URLS` which the tool reads automatically; this parameter is for cases where the agent wants to seed additional URLs at runtime (e.g. after recon discovers an admin panel).

parameter.name: openapi_url
parameter.description: OpenAPI 2.x or 3.x spec URL (JSON only — YAML not supported in the sandbox). When set, paths from the spec are seeded into the crawl. CLI: `--openapi` sets `STRIX_OPENAPI_URL` which the tool reads automatically.

returns.description:
{success, target, started_at, ended_at, seed_urls, openapi_url, config, endpoints: [{url, method, depth, discovered_via}], forms: [{url, method, action, fields}], js_bundles, errors, stats}.
`discovered_via` is one of: `seed` (initial URL), `html` (anchor / link), `form` (HTML form action), `js_bundle` (LinkFinder regex on JS source), `openapi` (path from the spec).
Always returns success=True even when individual fetches fail — failures are listed in `errors[]`.
